title: Fern leaf motif
subtitle: A pinnate fern frond with paired side leaflets, 14 cm
excerpt: The fern frond is the most architecturally complex of the leaf motifs: a long centre spine with six to eight pairs of small leaflet branches worked outward at regular intervals. The construction is the same as the oak leaf spine but repeated at a miniature scale for each leaflet. At 14 cm in DK cotton the frond is long enough for a large cushion centrepiece.
sourceNotes: Weldon's Practical Crochet, Volume 7 (1892), fern and botanical applique chapter (Internet Archive). Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopedia of Needlework (1886), crochet fern frond section.
heroPrompt: A crochet fern frond applique in mid-green DK cotton, 14 cm long with six pairs of small leaflet branches, photographed flat on natural linen in soft daylight.

chartDefinition.title: Fern leaf motif
chartDefinition.caption: Long centre spine chain. Paired leaflet branches at regular intervals: ch-6 out, 5 stitches of increasing height and return, sl-st back to spine. Six leaflet pairs from base to tip.

glossaryTerms.definition: A botanical term for a leaf with paired side leaflets along a centre midrib, like a fern frond. The crochet version replicates this structure with branch chains.

content.text: The fern frond is
pinnate

— a long centre spine with paired leaflets branching at each side. Each leaflet is a chain arch worked outward from the spine, stitched along its length (dc at the base, htr at the middle, dc at the tip), then slip stitched back to the spine chain to continue. The leaflets closest to the base are smallest; the middle leaflets are widest. The tip leaflet is a single spine-end rounded point.

attrs.title: Materials for one frond
attrs.body: About 10 g of mid-green DK cotton. A 4 mm hook. Tapestry needle. Scissors.

content.text: Gauge
Each finished fern frond measures 14 cm long and 6 cm wide at the widest pair of leaflets in DK-weight cotton with a 4 mm hook.
Stitches used
chain (ch), slip stitch (sl st) — UK and US shared.
double crochet (dc) — UK; US "single crochet".
half treble (htr) — UK; US "half double crochet".
Pattern
Spine
Ch 30. Sl st into 2nd and 3rd ch from hook (stem). The 28 remaining chains form the spine.
Leaflets — work along spine toward tip

At each leaflet position (every 4th chain along the spine), work the following for a right leaflet: Ch 6. Dc in 2nd ch from hook. Htr. Htr. Dc. Dc. Sl st back to the starting spine chain. For the left leaflet from the same spine position: Ch 6. Dc. Htr. Htr. Dc. Dc. Sl st back. Sl st along the spine 4 chains toward the tip. Repeat for 5 more pairs of leaflets (6 pairs total, increasing leaflet length toward the middle by adding 1-2 extra ch on the outer 2 pairs). At the spine tip, work 3dc to round the frond end. Sl st back along the spine underside to the stem. Fasten off.

definition.title: Fern leaf motif
definition.caption: 30ch spine. Six paired leaflets: ch-6 arches with dc/htr/dc stitches. Leaflets widen toward the middle. 3dc tip at frond end.

content.text: Finishing
Weave in all ends. Steam-block flat, pressing the leaflets open. Sew the frond onto the base fabric through the spine edge.
Care
Handwash in cool water. Re-steam-block the leaflets flat after washing.
What to try next

The ivy leaf (crochet-leaf-ivy) uses the same centre spine approach but with a simpler heart-shaped outline. The willow tree motif (crochet-willow-tree-motif) extends the drooping-branch idea to a larger tree composition.
